title: Odile and the Cipher
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Vane, founder of the lakeside town of Merrow's Bend, is exhumed for a cemetery relocation, insurance investigator Elodie Kavanagh is called in because her photographic memory once exposed a fraudulent death claim — and she instantly notices the burial records were altered decades ago. Her investigation reveals that Vane never died in 1962; he vanished, and four prominent families have been paying into a trust ever since to keep his disappearance buried, literally. As Elodie deciphers coded letters hidden in the town archive, she discovers Vane is still alive, hidden in plain sight as the town's aging archivist, and that one of the four heirs has begun killing anyone who might expose the secret. In the end, Elodie must choose between protecting the fragile identity of a man who built a community on a lie and telling the truth that will save an innocent suspect from execution — and she chooses truth, at the cost of her own hard-won belonging in Merrow's Bend.
about_author: Orsen Pemberton is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent seven years covering municipal archives and cold cases across the Great Lakes region. Pemberton now writes mysteries full-time from a farmhouse overlooking water, insisting that every fictional town be built from real minutes of real town council meetings.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Ground
chapters.summary: Elodie Kavanagh attends the exhumation of Aldous Vane as a formality for the cemetery relocation policy, only to watch the coffin rise empty. POV: Elodie. The emotional beat is quiet vertigo — her gift for detail, usually a comfort, becomes a curse as every impossible inconsistency imprints itself permanently in her mind.

chapters.title: Four Signatures
chapters.summary: Elodie pulls the original 1962 burial permit and, using her memory of handwriting samples from town hall, proves two signatures were forged after the fact. POV: Elodie, with flashbacks to her first solved 'accident.' The beat is mounting suspicion as she realizes the forgery required someone with access spanning generations.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes Itself
chapters.summary: Elodie interviews the descendants of the founding families, who close ranks with practiced warmth. The Harrow matriarch offers her a job, a house, and friendship — clearly a bribe. POV: alternating between Elodie and Daniel Vane-Byrne, the founder's great-grandson. The beat is seduction of belonging versus the itch of truth.

chapters.title: Letters in the Margins
chapters.summary: In the town archive, Elodie finds marginalia in the ledgers written in a substitution cipher she recognizes from a previous case. The ciphered notes reference 'the arrangement' and dates matching the forged permits. POV: Elodie. The beat is exhilaration curdling into fear when she realizes someone has recently removed pages — someone who knew she'd come.

chapters.title: The Drowning That Wasn't
chapters.summary: A retired deputy who helped falsify the 1962 record dies in a boating 'accident' hours before Elodie's scheduled interview with him. POV: the dying deputy first, then Elodie arriving too late. The beat is grief and guilt — her investigation has become a countdown, and the killer is ahead of her.

chapters.title: A Face She Has Seen Before
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing decades of town photographs in her memory, Elodie notices the same unremarkable face recurring across sixty years under three different names — always near the archive. The current archivist, Mr. Fenwick. POV: Elodie. The beat is the uncanny thrill of pattern recognition becoming personal recognition.

chapters.title: The Man Who Built Merrow's Bend
chapters.summary: Elodie confronts Fenwick privately; he confesses he is Aldous Vane, who faked his death to escape his partners' crimes and then spent a lifetime secretly shaping the town into something honest. POV: split between Elodie and Vane's confession. The beat is devastating empathy — the lie she must expose is also the town's soul.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Silence
chapters.summary: Vane identifies which heir has been silencing people: not to protect him, but because the trust pays out only while his death stands — and one heir has been skimming it for years. POV: Daniel Vane-Byrne, realizing his own father is implicated. The beat is loyalty fracturing along bloodlines as the noose tightens around an innocent scapegoat.

chapters.title: Cipher at the Waterline
chapters.summary: The killer lures Elodie to the boathouse with a final ciphered note and tries to drown her as the 'fourth accident.' Using her total recall of the boathouse layout from a single prior visit, she turns the trap, survives, and captures the confession on tape. POV: Elodie. The beat is terror transmuted into triumph through the very mind everyone underestimated.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: The truth goes public: Vane testifies, the guilty heir is arrested, and the town reels as its founding myth dissolves. Vane chooses exile; the townspeople turn their grief on Elodie, the outsider who broke them open. POV: Elodie, packing her car at dawn. The final beat is bittersweet resolve — she lost the town but kept herself, and somewhere new needs solving.
